title: Stream-slab framing, chunk ancestry, and graceful reconnect compatibility
creator: Priya Shah
description:
Goal: Implement a robust SSE-compatible streaming wire protocol variant ("stream-slab framing") that provides: 1) micro-chunked messages with chunk ancestry and idempotent chunk IDs for safe replay, 2) a reconnect handshake that allows gaps to be patched without duplicating tool/function-call boundaries, and 3) a backward-compatible shim for legacy clients that expect plain text/event-stream with no resume tokens.

Scope: implement server-side framing and resume token encoding, client-server handshake for resume (resume-token or last-ack model), chunk ancestry metadata, function-call atomicity markers, and a compatibility path that downgrades to legacy SSE semantics when negotiated. Add integration tests, end-to-end load tests, telemetry (resumes, duplicate-chunk-rate, reassembly-latency), and a rollout plan with canary percentages and automatic fallback.

Why: Current experiments with continuous output show replay and duplication issues when reconnects happen during function-call frames and structured JSONL fragments. Existing implementations either force long replays or risk half-applied tool calls. This ticket aims to balance safety and latency for customer-facing streaming APIs while minimizing client migration friction.
tasks: Design: finalize stream-slab wire format and resume token (metadata encoding, sequence numbers, ancestry) - design doc PR
Server: add framing encoder/decoder that emits length-prefixed micro-chunks with chunk-id and parent-id headers
Server: implement reconnect handshake endpoint and resume token validation with gap healing logic
Server: ensure function-call atomicity markers are emitted and reassembly enforces atomic application of tool calls
Compatibility shim: implement 'legacy-mode' toggle that translates slab chunks to text/event-stream events for old clients
Client: add resume token handling in JS SDK and Go SDK (non-blocking) - feature flag behind runtime-2.4
Testing: unit tests for chunk ordering, replay, duplicate suppression, and function-call boundaries
Load tests: end-to-end reconnect storm test with 50k stream restarts/hour using staging cluster
Metrics: add resume_attempt, resume_success, duplicate_chunk_rate, reassembly_time, functioncall_replay_count
Rollout: phased canary 1% -> 10% -> 50% with automated rollback on duplicate_chunk_rate > 0.5%
acceptance_criteria: A resume handshake that allows a client to supply a resume token and the server to return an explicit gap plan (missing-seqs or ack)
No duplication of function-call application observed in end-to-end tests (0 false-positive tool calls across 100k reconnects)
Legacy clients (text/event-stream consumers) continue to receive coherent event ordering when negotiated; no client-side change required for >=90% of existing customers
Metrics emitted and visible in Console: resume_attempt, resume_success, duplicate_chunk_rate, reassembly_time
Automated rollback triggers and canary ramp documented and exercised in staging runbook
comments: 2026-02-11 Priya Shah: Kicked off spike. Prototype wire format in docs/confluence: /d/StreamSlab-Design. Initial trade-offs: length-prefixing vs JSONL chunking. We prefer length-prefixing for binary-safety and unambiguous boundaries.

2026-02-18 Carlos Mendes: Implemented encoder/decoder prototype in runtime branch feature/stream-slab. See PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2417. Early perf looks good: framing overhead ~0.7% on p3.2x latency p50 unchanged.

2026-02-22 Design review (Anya Li): Concern about resume token leakage. Decided to encrypt resume tokens with customer key fingerprint and TTL. Action: add KMS wrapping for tokens for Private deployments.

2026-02-25 Eng sync: Resolved function-call atomicity by introducing 'fc_start' and 'fc_end' chunk labels and enforcing reassembly ordering before emitting tool calls. Edge-case: partial fc_end missing on reconnect -> server returns 'patch' that includes the missing chunks or an explicit NACK requiring client to re-issue the function call. Chosen approach: server-supplied patch where feasible, otherwise NACK + client retry.
2026-03-01 QA: Added failing test where client reconnects mid-token and receives duplicate fc application. Investigating duplicate suppression logic in reassembly layer.
2026-03-04 Security: SSO and token wrapping reviewed. Security requested additional audit logs for resume token minting and consumption. Filed follow-up ENG-520010 for audit log schema changes.

2026-03-05 Carlos Mendes: Fixed duplicate suppression bug (race in chunk-pointer advance). Deployed patched canary to staging. Re-run reconnect storm shows duplicate_chunk_rate reduced from 0.9% -> 0.03%.
2026-03-05 PM review (Dylan Park): Approved rollout plan pending KMS integration for Private customers. Requested that we add a migration note in SDK changelog and Console alerts for resumed streams.
2026-03-05 Design sign-off (Anya Li): UX for client-visible resume errors finalized. Added human-readable codes: RESUME_OK, RESUME_PATCHED, RESUME_NACK, RESUME_EXPIRED.
notes: Migration considerations: SDKs will expose resume token handling behind a feature flag. We will provide a compatibility guide showing how clients can opt-in to the slab format for stronger resume guarantees. For Private deployments, resume tokens will be KMS-wrapped; runtime will detect missing KMS and fall back to legacy mode with a warning. Track rollout with console alert on duplicate_chunk_rate > 0.25%.
